summary: This work demonstrates parity lifetimes exceeding 20 s in InAs–Pb tetron devices via interferometric readout, representing a $>1000	imes$ improvement over Al-based tetrons and validating that larger superconducting gap directly suppresses quasiparticle poisoning errors. The authors introduce rf-based wire spectroscopy to measure Majorana splitting $E_M < 1$ µeV with $μ$eV precision and identify operating regimes where both Majorana hybridization and non-equilibrium poisoning are strongly suppressed.
motivation: Topological qubits based on Majorana zero modes promise exponentially suppressed error rates with increasing topological gap, but this principle has not been experimentally validated at the qubit level. The authors sought to test whether replacing Al (gap $\Delta_{\text{Pb}} \approx 1.3$ meV versus $\Delta_{\text{Al}} \approx 300$ µeV) with Pb and optimizing the semiconductor heterostructure on GaSb substrate would yield measurable improvements in device robustness.
method: The work employs a multi-tetron array with optimized InAs–Pb hybrid structure exhibiting topological gap $\Delta_T \sim 70$ µeV (versus $\sim 30$ µeV in Al devices) and spin-orbit coupling $\alpha \sim 12$–16 meV·nm. An rf-based parity injection spectroscopy technique measures low-energy wire-end states with $\sim 1$ µeV resolution by coupling quantum dots to both ends of the nanowire in an interferometric configuration. Parity lifetimes are extracted from telegraph noise in quantum-capacitance time traces following controlled electron injection via QD4.
result: Characteristic $Z$-parity switching time is $\tau_Z = 22 ± 1$ s with some traces reaching minute-scale, compared to 1–12 ms in Al-based tetrons—a $>1000\times$ enhancement. The measured Majorana splitting remains $E_M < 1$ µeV across extended parameter regimes, and the parity lifetime substantially exceeds typical qubit operation times ($\sim 1$ µs), suggesting that qubit operations are no longer limited by quasiparticle poisoning.
